title: What does MAS DPT AML rules mean for agent payments?
abstract: Sourced explanation of MAS DPT AML rules and its practical limits.
body:
According to MAS, MAS Notice PSN02 requires covered digital payment token service providers to maintain AML and counter-terrorist-financing controls. [1]

MAS lists customer due diligence, risk assessment, record keeping, suspicious-transaction reporting and internal compliance arrangements among the requirements. The notice includes beneficial-owner identification and ongoing review, not merely checking a wallet against a static address list. An accepted XRPL Credential can carry an attestation, but it does not by itself demonstrate that a provider has fulfilled those operational and legal duties. [1]

For an agent payment service, assess the parties, control over funds and actual service before drawing a legal conclusion about MAS DPT AML rules. Testnet execution demonstrates a mechanism with faucet assets; it does not establish licensing, safeguarding or real-customer compliance. A small payment or an automated decision is not evidence of an exemption. The cited authority describes a framework, not a legal opinion about this product. [1]

Author interpretation: map the proposed business flow to the current rules with qualified local advice, preserve the basis for each conclusion and revisit it when the flow changes. Keep personal information out of public ledger memos and use appropriate private channels for necessary information exchange. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
